description:
Find claims from a natural-language question.

    The central research concept and its scientific synonyms outrank incidental context words. Generic overlap that does not address the question is penalized. A keyword with no function word stays on the lexical match.
    A question tries its content phrases first. When that match is thin, extracted concepts, shorter phrases, and synonyms are combined and deduplicated before ranking. Exact keywords are not required.
    Question hits stay on strategy question. fallback is null when the content-phrase match already addressed the concept, keyword when every hit came from a literal concept or shorter phrase, and expanded when a synonym supplied a hit. Rank puts the concept above context words. Retrieval relevance stays ahead of evidence_strength, and match_reason records that the stored score is evidence_strength. A lexical phrase matches whole tokens. K17, PDAC, NCC, IIT, and LLM match the full names in the alias map.
    notice is no_matching_claims when nothing matches. notice is no_evidence when every returned hit has an empty excerpt. A hit with an empty excerpt says no evidence in match_reason.
    exploratory true keeps matches under the default relevance threshold.
    Each hit includes match_reason, source_url, doi, and paper_id when those are known, up to two supporting claims, and one contradicting claim when one is stored. Each related claim carries that same compact pointer. unpublished is true for a private unpublished paper. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
    status_note on a consensus claim with no stored contradiction is: No stored contradiction; not independent multi-source consensus.
    evidence_note is: Extractor confidence in the claim statement, not study quality.
    integrity_warning is set when the statement unit looks truncated relative to the excerpt, or the magnitude looks extreme relative to the excerpt. The statement and the excerpt are not rewritten.

    A domain keeps claims whose primary domain is that value or one of its
    aliases. cross_domain also keeps claims from other domains that carry
    the domain as a secondary tag.

    Use this when the input is a question instead of keywords.
    Example: search_smart(natural_language="How do transformers handle long context?", domain="ai-ml", limit=5).
    Example: search_smart(natural_language="What causes LLM hallucinations in RAG systems?", limit=5).

cross_domain.description: Also return claims from other primary domains that carry this domain as a secondary tag. Default false.
cross_domain.title: Cross Domain

domain.description: Primary domain or an alias of it. Example: ai-ml.
domain.title: Domain

exploratory.description: Keep weaker matches that miss the central concept. Default false applies a light relevance threshold.
exploratory.title: Exploratory

natural_language.description: A question or description of the claims you want. Example: How do transformers handle long context?
examples: How do transformers handle long context?
natural_language.title: Natural Language

offset.description: Number of hits to skip. Example: 0.
offset.title: Offset

name: search_smart

contradicting.description: One stored contradicting claim, when one is present, with the same compact source pointer.

doi.description: Stored DOI, the DataCite DOI of an arXiv id, or a bioRxiv paper id that is already a DOI. Empty when unknown. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
doi.title: Doi

evidence_note.description: Extractor confidence in the claim statement, not study quality. evidence_strength is that extractor confidence.
evidence_note.title: Evidence Note

integrity_warning.description: Set when the statement unit looks truncated relative to the excerpt, or the magnitude looks extreme relative to the excerpt. The statement and the excerpt are not rewritten.
integrity_warning.title: Integrity Warning

match_reason.description: Why this hit ranked here: keyword overlap, domain match, and retrieval relevance. evidence_strength is the stored score and is named here. The number stays on evidence_strength.
match_reason.title: Match Reason

paper_id.description: Stored paper id when one is known. A private paper is an opaque private-paper id. Empty when unknown. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
paper_id.title: Paper Id

source_url.description: Stable link to the paper when one is known. Empty when the claim has no pointer. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
source_url.title: Source Url

status_note.description: Set on a consensus claim with no stored contradiction: No stored contradiction; not independent multi-source consensus. Null for contested, outdated, or a claim that already has a contradiction.
status_note.title: Status Note

supporting.description: Up to two other claims from the same papers. Each has claim_id, statement, strength, and the same compact source pointer.
supporting.title: Supporting

unpublished.description: True when this claim is from a private unpublished paper. Public sources stay false.
unpublished.title: Unpublished

RelatedClaim.description: One claim shown beside a search hit.

doi.description: Stored DOI, the DataCite DOI of an arXiv id, or a bioRxiv paper id that is already a DOI. Empty when unknown.
doi.title: Doi

paper_id.description: Stored paper id. A private paper is an opaque private-paper id. Empty when unknown.
paper_id.title: Paper Id

relationship_basis.description: Why this related claim is shown. same_source means the same paper and is not independent evidence. lexical, methodological, transfer, and contradiction name the other stored signals. Null when unknown.

source_url.description: Stable link to that claim's paper when one is known. Empty when it has no pointer.
source_url.title: Source Url

unpublished.description: True when that claim is from a private unpublished paper.
unpublished.title: Unpublished

RelatedClaim.title: RelatedClaim

RelationshipBasis.description:
Why two claims were linked.

An older stored row omits this field and still loads as null. Scoring
never returns null. ``reclassify_stored_flags`` writes a basis onto
every row it can score, and writes lexical onto a null row it cannot
score. That fallback is explicit: the enum has no conceptual value, so
overlap that is not a bound technique, a stated transfer, a stored
contradiction, or the same paper is lexical. It is not upgraded.

same_source is the same paper and is not independent evidence.
lexical is shared vocabulary, including a generic label.
methodological is a technique bound to a shared specific noun.
transfer is a mechanism the claims state. contradiction is a stored disagreement.
RelationshipBasis.title: RelationshipBasis

outputSchema.description:
question matches a research concept. lexical is a keyword query.

fallback is keyword when a literal concept or shorter phrase supplied
every hit, and expanded when a scientific synonym supplied one. It is
null when the content-phrase match already addressed the concept.
notice is no_matching_claims when the query matches nothing, and
no_evidence when every returned hit has an empty excerpt.
partial_concepts means the returned claims do not cover every mandatory
concept. missing_concepts names what that returned text does not fully hold.
A claim that contains every concept does not set the notice.

fallback.description: keyword when a literal concept or shorter phrase supplied every hit. expanded when a scientific synonym supplied one. Null when the query is lexical, or when the content-phrase match already addressed the concept.
fallback.title: Fallback

missing_concepts.description: Mandatory concepts the returned claim text does not fully hold. Taken from those hits, not from expanded search phrases. Empty unless notice is partial_concepts.
missing_concepts.title: Missing Concepts

notice.description: no_matching_claims when the query matches nothing. no_evidence when every returned hit has an empty excerpt. partial_concepts when the returned claims do not cover every mandatory concept. A claim that contains every concept does not set it. Null when the query is not multi-concept, when a returned claim covers every concept, or when nothing was returned.
notice.title: Notice

strategy.description: question for a natural-language question. lexical for a keyword or a phrase with no function word.
strategy.title: Strategy

outputSchema.title: SmartSearchResult
